Build a Co-occurrence Network

Source: R/co_occurrence.R
cooccurrence.Rd

cooccurrence() builds an undirected network of items that appear together in the same transaction (a document, a session, a record): an edge joins two items that occur together, weighted by how often they do, or by a similarity measure that adjusts that count for how often each item occurs overall. With similarity = "relative" the network is directed. It reads delimited columns (keywords separated by ";"), a long table of items per transaction, a 0/1 incidence table, wide sequences or a list of transactions; the Details say how each is recognised.

Raw counts grow with how frequent the two items are, so the most frequent items dominate a count network. The similarity measures correct for that in different ways (van Eck & Waltman, 2009); compare a few before reading which pairs are strongest. The network is descriptive: it keeps no source data, so bootstrap_network() and permutation() cannot resample it.

Usage

cooccurrence(
  data,
  field = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  sep = NULL,
  similarity = c("none", "jaccard", "cosine", "inclusion", "association", "dice",
    "equivalence", "relative"),
  threshold = 0,
  min_occur = 1L,
  diagonal = TRUE,
  top_n = NULL,
  ...,
  format = c("auto", "binary")
)

Arguments

data

The transactions, in one of these forms:

  • a data frame with a delimited column (field and sep);

  • a data frame in long (bipartite) form, one row per item in a transaction (field and by);

  • a 0/1 or TRUE/FALSE data frame or matrix, one row per transaction and one column per item, declared with format = "binary";

  • a wide sequence data frame or matrix with other values, whose rows are the transactions;

  • a plain list of character vectors, one per transaction.

A network object (netobject, netobject_group, cograph_network, tna) raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input; pass the data it was built from.

field

The column holding the items, which become the nodes. With sep, its values are split by sep; several column names pool the split values of each row. With by, it is the item column of a long table. Default NULL. Setting by or sep without field, or field without either, raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input, as does naming a column that data does not have, or setting any of the three for a list.

by

The column that defines the transactions of a long table: each of its values is one transaction, holding the distinct field values of its rows (for example "paper_id" or "session_id"). Default NULL, where items co-occur within the same row. Ignored when sep is set, which reads field as delimited.

sep

The separator that splits delimited field values, such as ";" or ",", matched literally; the split values are trimmed. Default NULL. See field for the combinations that raise an error.

similarity

How the co-occurrence count \(C_{ij}\) of items \(i\) and \(j\), with item frequencies \(f_i\) and \(f_j\), is turned into an edge weight. Default "none".

"none"

Raw co-occurrence counts.

"jaccard"

\(C_{ij} / (f_i + f_j - C_{ij})\).

"cosine"

\(C_{ij} / \sqrt{f_i \cdot f_j}\) (Salton's cosine).

"inclusion"

\(C_{ij} / \min(f_i, f_j)\) (Simpson coefficient).

"association"

\(C_{ij} / (f_i \cdot f_j)\) (association strength, or probabilistic affinity index; van Eck & Waltman, 2009).

"dice"

\(2 C_{ij} / (f_i + f_j)\).

"equivalence"

\(C_{ij}^2 / (f_i \cdot f_j)\) (Salton's cosine squared).

"relative"

Each row divided by its sum (the diagonal included when diagonal = TRUE), so each row sums to 1: the weight from i to j is the share of i's co-occurrences that involve j. The matrix is no longer symmetric, so the network is directed and both directions of a pair are edges.

A zero denominator is replaced by 1, so an item without co-occurrences gets weight 0 rather than NaN.

threshold

The smallest weight kept: weights below it, on the scale of similarity, are set to zero. Default 0 (none).

min_occur

The fewest transactions an item must appear in to be kept. Rarer items are dropped before the co-occurrences are counted, and transactions left empty are dropped with them. Default 1 (keep all).

diagonal

Whether the diagonal is kept. With TRUE (default) it holds each item's frequency (the number of transactions it appears in), transformed by similarity; with FALSE it is set to zero. Item frequencies for the similarity measures are the same either way.

top_n

How many of the strongest off-diagonal edges to keep: pairs in an undirected network, directed cells with similarity = "relative". Edges tied with the top_n-th weight are all kept, so a few more may remain, and the diagonal is not affected. Default NULL (all edges).

...

Not used.

format

How 0/1 columns are read. Columns of only 0 and 1 (or TRUE and FALSE) could be items or recoded positions, so with "auto" (default) they raise an error of class nestimate_bad_input. "binary" declares them items, one row per transaction, where a missing cell counts as no occurrence; it raises the same error on data with any other value.

Value

A netobject (class c("netobject", "cograph_network")), undirected (directed with similarity = "relative"), with method = "co_occurrence_fn". Print it for an overview; extract_edges() gives one row per edge, extract_transition_matrix() the weight matrix (one row and column per item kept), net_centrality() the node centralities, and cograph::splot() draws it. It is built without build_network() and holds no source data (data is NULL). Its params record similarity, threshold, min_occur, diagonal, top_n, n_transactions and n_items.

Details

Six input forms are recognised from data and from which of field, by and sep are set:

  1. Delimited: field (one column) and sep. Each cell is split by sep, trimmed, and its distinct values form a transaction.

  2. Multi-column delimited: field (several columns) and sep. The split values of a row's columns are pooled into one transaction.

  3. Long bipartite: field and by. The distinct field values within each by group form a transaction.

  4. Binary: none of the three, all values 0/1 or logical, and format = "binary". Columns are items, rows are transactions; a missing cell is no occurrence. Without format = "binary" such data is refused, since 0/1 columns could also be recoded positions.

  5. Wide sequence: none of the three, other values. The distinct states of each row form a transaction, leaving out missing values and the void markers ("%", "*", "", "NA", "NaN"). A data frame must be a single column or a numbered run of position columns (T1, T2, ...) with nothing beside it; any other frame raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input, and a column called action and repeated column names are refused the same way.

  6. List: a plain list of character vectors.

To count co-occurrence of states within sequences through build_network(), with its resampling verbs, use build_network(method = "co_occurrence") or build_cna() instead.

All forms are turned into a list of transactions, which min_occur filters. The raw counts are crossprod(B) of the binary transaction matrix B; similarity is applied to them, then threshold, then top_n.

References

van Eck, N. J., & Waltman, L. (2009). How to normalize co-occurrence data? An analysis of some well-known similarity measures. Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology, 60(8), 1635–1651.

See also

build_cna for sequence-positional co-occurrence via build_network().

Examples

# Delimited field (e.g., keyword co-occurrence)
df <- data.frame(
  id = 1:4,
  keywords = c("network; graph", "graph; matrix; network",
               "matrix; algebra", "network; algebra; graph")
)
net <- cooccurrence(df, field = "keywords", sep = ";")

# Long/bipartite
long_df <- data.frame(
  paper = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3),
  keyword = c("network", "graph", "matrix", "graph", "algebra",
              "network", "algebra")
)
net <- cooccurrence(long_df, field = "keyword", by = "paper")

# List of transactions
transactions <- list(c("A", "B"), c("B", "C"), c("A", "B", "C"))
net <- cooccurrence(transactions, similarity = "jaccard")

# Binary matrix
bin <- matrix(c(1,0,1, 1,1,0, 0,1,1), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE,
              dimnames = list(NULL, c("X", "Y", "Z")))
net <- cooccurrence(bin, format = "binary")
